thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: surge of errors observed in GCP networking control plane affecting cross-region routing for Private VPC deployments. 5m error rate: 12% (502/504/429) on ILB controlplane calls. Affected regions: us-west1 -> us-east1 path. Paging SRE oncall (Maya).
Maya: ack, I'm on call. Starting triage. @Ravi please check GCP forwarding-rules / target proxies and any quota errors.
Ravi: looking now. I'm seeing a lot of 429/RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED from the ForwardingRules API when we try to fetch forwarding-rule state for private-vpc projects. Logs show bursts around 11:03-11:12 UTC. 429s coincide with our route-sync job spikes.
Maya: noted. Did the route-sync run recently?
Ravi: yes, auto-sync ran at 11:02 for a scheduled rollout. The job retried aggressively; GCP started rate-limiting subsequent GETs.
Jon: I can confirm ILB proxy reports connection resets and healthcheck failures correlated with missing forwarding-rule reads. This is causing cross-region routing to degrade because we can't resolve remote endpoints.
Lena: suggestion: temporarily disable cross-region route-sync for Private VPC projects and fall back to local-region-only routing until GCP restores API quota. We have a runtime switch: `routing.cross_region_sync=false` for the router agent.
Maya: let's do that as a quick mitigation. Ravi, can you flip the switch for affected projects? Which ones are impacted?
Ravi: running query to list impacted projects: `gcloud projects list --filter="labels:private-vpc" --format="value(projectId)" | xargs -n1 ./tools/check-route-sync` returns: redwood-priv-101, acme-enterprise-2, finco-prod. I'll disable cross-region sync for those three first.
Ravi: applying change now. Command: ```
kubectl -n router-system set env deployment/router AGENT_FLAGS='--cross-region-sync=false' --selector app=router
```
Ravi: patch applied to router agents in us-west1 and us-east1. Rolling restart in progress.
Priya: Customer success ping: acme-enterprise-2 reported elevated 5xxs to support@acme. I'm sending them an interim note: "We're aware of cross-region routing errors impacting Private VPCs; we've applied a temporary routing fallback to reduce cross-region calls while we work with GCP. Expect improved stability in ~10-15 minutes."
Carlos: can we also enable prefix caching for KV cache to lower route-sync read volume? We have a config to increase cache TTL: `ROUTE_CACHE_TTL=300` -> `600`. That will reduce API pressure.
Lena: applying KV cache TTL bump now for router service. Patch: `env: ROUTE_CACHE_TTL=600`.
incident-bot: Created ticket with GCP support: INC-2023-12345. Severity: High. Contact: GCP NOC.
Maya: I opened the GCP support case as well with logs and requests to review forwarding-rules API throttles. Attached: `forwarding-rules-429.log` and sample call stacks.
GCP Support: We've received your escalation. Initial investigation shows an internal rate-limiter triggered in the forwarding-rules control plane for us-west1 due to bursty metadata reads. We're looking at short-term mitigation on our side and will follow up in the case. Recommend backoff/retry and reduce read fanout.
Maya: thanks. On our side we've disabled cross-region sync and increased route cache TTL; we've also added exponential backoff to the route-sync job. Monitoring metrics now.
Jon: after the mitigation I'm seeing a reduction in 5xxs for the affected customers. Error rate dropped from 12% -> ~3% over the last 7 minutes. Healthchecks for ILBs are stabilizing.
Priya: sending updated customer note to the three customers with ETA. message draft: ```Hi — we're actively responding to an infrastructure issue affecting Private VPC cross-region routing. We've applied a temporary configuration to reduce cross-region calls which should restore stability. We'll provide ETA within 30 minutes and a detailed post-incident summary. — Priya (CS)```
Maya: planning handoff: I need to step off in 20m. Jon, can you take second-shift oncall and keep the channel warm? If GCP has no mitigation in 30m escalate to L3 and re-enable route-sync cautiously.
Jon: taking handoff. I'll stay on for the next 2 hours. If error rate creeps back above 5% I'll open an internal escalation and route to L3.
Ravi: monitoring network metrics and route-sync retry counters. Current notable counters: forwarding_rule_429_count=842 (1h window), route_sync_retry_rate=18/min. I'll keep an eye and revert changes only after GCP confirms control plane is healthy.
Maya: logging post-incident tasks: 1) add rate-limiter-aware backoff to route-sync 2) add per-project sync jitter 3) automate temporary disable + rollback runbook 4) customer comms template.
Carlos: I'll pick up task #2 and #3. I'll create a PR with jitter implementation and a CLI to orchestrate an emergency disable/enable.
Priya: CS will log a support escalation bundle for the three impacted customers and track follow-ups.
GCP Support: Update: we've opened a backend ticket, applying service-side mitigation in us-west1; we expect reductions in 15-30 minutes. We'll post case updates.
Maya: status update for SEV board: partial mitigation in place, customer impact reduced, GCP engaged. Keeping incident open. Handoff to Jon in 15m.
Jon: ack. I'll wait for GCP confirmation. If service-side fix doesn't land in 40m we'll consider rolling back the scheduled route-sync rollout that triggered the burst.
incident-bot: :white_check_mark: STATUS CHANGE: error rate down to 3% for the last 10m. Severity lowered to S3. Keep monitoring for 60 minutes before auto-close.
Maya: handoff complete — leaving channel. @Jon you own this.
Jon: I have it. Will update on any regressions.
Priya: Customer updates sent. I'll prepare the incident blameless postmortem template once we close.
